stories.title: Sports roundup: Tribunal freezes Mariga's FKF expulsion, DCI and ADAK team up on doping, Fernandes stays at United
key_points: The Sports Disputes Tribunal has suspended the expulsion of FKF deputy president McDonald Mariga and six others.
The DCI and the anti-doping agency ADAK signed a deal to hunt down doping networks.
Victor Wanyama has taken over Nairobi City Stars, Pulse Sports reported, citing an insider.
Manchester United extended Bruno Fernandes' contract to 2028 before facing Brentford today.
stories.content:
Here is the top sports news of the last two days, starting with Kenya.

Tribunal freezes Mariga's expulsion from FKF

The Sports Disputes Tribunal (SDT) on Friday suspended the expulsion of Football Kenya Federation (FKF) deputy president McDonald Mariga and six other National Executive Committee members, The Star reported.

The seven were expelled at an FKF special general meeting in Meru on November 7. The others are Gabriel Mghendi, Collins Kalee, Daniel Shikanda, Bernard Lagat, Robert Macharia and Kerubo Momanyi. On November 25, the High Court in Siaya dismissed their case, saying they had not first used the football body's own dispute system. FKF then named seven interim members, including Caleb Amwayi as deputy president.

Mariga went to the tribunal on November 26. The tribunal has now suspended both the Meru resolutions and the interim appointments until it hears both sides. FKF must reply by December 4, and the case returns on December 8. The Star noted this is temporary relief and does not decide who is right.

DCI and ADAK join forces against doping

The Directorate of Criminal Investigations (DCI) and the Anti-Doping Agency of Kenya (ADAK) signed an agreement on Friday in Nairobi to share information and investigate doping networks together, The Star reported. DCI Director Mohamed Amin and ADAK chief executive Peninah Wahome attended.

The deal comes after several Kenyan runners were banned. These include marathon star Peres Jepchirchir, who got a three-year ban for the banned substance EPO, The Star said.

Wanyama takes over City Stars

Former Harambee Stars captain Victor Wanyama has taken over ownership of Nairobi City Stars from businessman Jonathan Jackson, Pulse Sports reported on Friday, citing an insider. We reported on Friday that he was linked with the deal. No price was given, and there was no official club statement in the reports we read. City Stars play in the National Super League and have had money problems. Pulse said the plan is to win promotion back to the FKF Premier League and build a youth system.

FKF Premier League

Tusker beat Posta Rangers 2-1 at Ruaraka on Thursday, with goals from Chris Erambo and Victor Mbaoma, according to The Star.

Europe: Fernandes stays, United face Brentford

Manchester United have used a clause in Bruno Fernandes' contract to keep him until the end of the 2027-28 season, Al Jazeera reported. He was in the last year of his deal.

United, under new manager Mauricio Pochettino, host Brentford at Old Trafford today, Saturday, at 3pm UK time (6pm in Kenya). Al Jazeera said United are second from bottom with eight points from 11 games, while Brentford are sixth with 17 points.

In the Europa League on Thursday, Juventus beat Omonia 4-1, AC Milan won 4-2 at Olympiakos and Bayer Leverkusen won 2-0 at Dinamo Zagreb, according to Xinhua. Before Marseille's 1-0 win over Levski Sofia, fans fought in the stadium. Five Bulgarian fans went to hospital, and French President Emmanuel Macron condemned the attacks, Al Jazeera reported.

FIFA hit by cyberattack

FIFA said it was the victim of a criminal cyberattack in which some personal and business information was taken. It did not say how many people were affected and said it is working with police, Al Jazeera reported.

stories.title: World roundup: UN warns of famine risk in Africa, Ukraine offers Black Sea ceasefire, migrant deaths off Canary Islands
key_points: UN food agencies list 16 hunger hotspots, including Sudan, South Sudan, Somalia, Uganda and Chad.
Ukraine offers Russia a ceasefire at sea to protect grain exports and waits for Moscow's answer.
At least eight people are found dead on a migrant boat near Spain's Canary Islands.
The US says it disabled another ship trying to break its blockade of Iran; at least 13 soldiers are killed in Niger.
stories.content:
Here are the biggest world stories of the last 24 hours, with a focus on news that matters to Africans and Kenyans abroad.

UN: hunger to get worse in 16 hotspots, many in Africa

Two UN agencies, the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) and the World Food Programme (WFP), said on Friday that hunger will get much worse in 16 places over the next six months, from December to May. That is up from 13 places in June, Al Jazeera reported.

Sudan, South Sudan, Somalia, northern Nigeria and Yemen face the most serious risk of famine. Chad, Uganda and parts of Southern Africa were added to the list. The agencies said war is the main cause of hunger in 12 of the 16 places. They also warned that the El Niño weather pattern is expected to become very strong.

According to the report, aid to the five worst-hit countries fell from $5.1 billion in 2022 to $2 billion in 2025.

What this means for Kenyans: three of Kenya's neighbours, Somalia, South Sudan and Uganda, are on the list, and El Niño can bring floods and crop losses to East Africa.

Ukraine offers a ceasefire at sea to protect grain

Ukraine has offered Russia a ceasefire in the Black Sea to protect ships carrying grain and other food. Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha announced the offer on Friday at a food conference. "We are now awaiting a response from Russia," he said, as quoted by Al Jazeera.

Al Jazeera reported that Russia wants oil shipping included, while Ukraine says oil belongs in a wider energy deal. On the same day, Russian President Vladimir Putin attended a ceremony for a new nuclear-powered submarine. Moscow says it carries hypersonic missiles.

What this means for Kenyans: Ukraine is a major grain exporter, and safe shipping helps keep world wheat and food prices stable, including in Africa.

At least eight dead on migrant boat near Canary Islands

Spain's sea rescue service said eight to 10 bodies were found on a boat carrying about 100 people near El Hierro in the Canary Islands on Friday, Al Jazeera reported. Six people were flown to hospital in serious condition.

The Canary Islands leader, Fernando Clavijo, said the emergency begins on the shores of Senegal and Gambia, and asked Madrid and the European Union to act. A record 2,100 people reached the islands in a single day earlier this week. Spain holds a general election on Sunday, and migration is a major issue.

US disables another ship near Iran

The US military said its forces fired on a Palau-flagged cargo ship, the Pacific Archer, in the Gulf of Oman and disabled its engine as it tried to break the US blockade of Iran. US Central Command said the crew was not hurt. Al Jazeera said this is at least the 15th ship publicly reported disabled since the blockade began in April.

Iran's Revolutionary Guards said one tanker hit a naval mine in the Strait of Hormuz. That claim has not been independently confirmed.

What this means for Kenyans: trouble in the Gulf shipping lanes can push up fuel prices, which affects transport and food costs at home.

At least 13 soldiers killed in Niger

Gunmen attacked a National Guard base in Sanam, in Niger's Tillabéri region near the border with Mali, early on Thursday. Niger's Defence Ministry said at least 13 soldiers were killed and 20 wounded, Al Jazeera reported. The ministry called it a terrorist attack. It was not clear who carried it out.

stories.title: Natembeya joins Sifuna in Dallas as Linda Mwananchi US tour moves to Houston, Seattle and California
key_points: Trans Nzoia Governor George Natembeya has joined Senator Edwin Sifuna's tour of Kenyan communities in the US.
Natembeya said he arrived in Dallas, Texas, on Friday, according to The Star.
Next stops are Houston, the Seattle area, San Francisco and Oakland, ending in Silicon Valley on December 7.
The team promises Kenyans abroad better consular services and cheaper remittances.
stories.content:
Trans Nzoia Governor George Natembeya has joined Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna on his tour of Kenyan communities in the United States. The tour is run by Sifuna's Linda Mwananchi movement ahead of the 2027 General Election.

According to The Star, Natembeya announced on social media that he arrived in Dallas, Texas, on Friday, November 27. The Star said Natembeya helps coordinate Sifuna's presidential campaign. The same day, back in Kenya, DAP-K party leader Eugene Wamalwa removed Natembeya as one of the party's deputy leaders, as we reported on Friday.

Where the tour has been

The tour started on November 21 and runs to December 7. Mwakilishi, a diaspora news site, reported these earlier stops:

  • Hackettstown, New Jersey (Nov 21): opening of the movement's first US office.
  • Allentown, Pennsylvania (Nov 22): a church service and a town hall.
  • Maryland and Washington DC (Nov 23–25): a community dinner and meetings with women's, youth and policy groups.

Vihiga Senator Godfrey Osotsi and former Meru Governor Kawira Mwangaza travelled with Sifuna on the first leg, Mwakilishi and Streamline reported.

Where the tour goes next

The published schedule, as reported by Mwakilishi and Capital FM, lists:

  • Houston, Texas (Nov 29): a women's caucus and a town hall.
  • Washington State, Seattle area (Dec 3–4): church services, a gala dinner and a town hall in Federal Way and Renton.
  • San Francisco and Oakland (Dec 5): a town hall in the afternoon and a gala dinner in the evening.
  • Silicon Valley (Dec 7): the closing dinner.

Times and places can change, so check with local organisers before you travel.

What the team is promising

Mwakilishi reported that the movement is promising Kenyans abroad:

  • a fully online, one-stop system for consular services, with clear timelines and tracking;
  • more staff and service points at Kenyan missions, and quick action on fraud reports;
  • lower remittance costs, below 3 percent, by removing taxes and paperwork;
  • a bigger say in government decisions, and wider voting access.

"We want your country to be there for you," Sifuna told diaspora Kenyans, according to Mwakilishi. Sifuna has also said his first rally after returning home will be in Eldoret, Capital FM reported.

The other side

Sifuna's main message is that the current government has neglected Kenyans abroad. The government has not responded to these claims in the reports we read. Earlier this week Sifuna answered critics of the tour, and US filings showed a plan to raise funds from the diaspora, as we reported on Thursday.

What you can do

  • If you want to attend: look for the event details shared by Kenyan community groups in Houston, Seattle or the Bay Area, and confirm the time and venue before you go.
  • Ask your own questions: town halls usually take questions, so prepare one on the issues that matter to you, such as passports, voting or remittances.
  • Check your voter status: diaspora Kenyans can currently vote only in the presidential election. Watch for IEBC announcements on diaspora voter registration before 2027.
  • Hear all sides: other leaders and parties also court the diaspora. Compare their plans before you decide.

stories.title: Former Migori Governor Okoth Obado jailed for 25 years over 2018 murder of Sharon Otieno
key_points: The High Court in Nairobi on Friday sentenced former Migori Governor Okoth Obado to 25 years in prison.
His former aide Michael Oyamo also got 25 years, and former county official Caspal Obiero got 18 years.
The three were found guilty in July of killing university student Sharon Otieno in September 2018.
The judge said time already spent in custody will count, and made no order for compensation.
stories.content:
Former Migori Governor Okoth Obado has been sentenced to 25 years in prison for the murder of university student Sharon Otieno in 2018. The sentence was given on Friday, November 27, at the High Court in Nairobi (Milimani), according to Citizen Digital and NTV.

The sentences

Justice Cecilia Githua sentenced three men:

  • Okoth Obado, former Governor of Migori County: 25 years.
  • Michael Juma Oyamo, his former personal assistant: 25 years.
  • Caspal Obiero, a former Migori County official: 18 years.

The Star reported that the time the three have already spent in custody will be counted as part of the sentence.

What happened in 2018

Sharon Otieno was a 26-year-old student at Rongo University. She was seven months pregnant when she was killed on September 3, 2018. Her body was found in a forest in Homa Bay County. She had been abducted together with a journalist, who escaped.

Citizen Digital and NTV reported that the court found the three men guilty of murder on July 23, 2026. NTV said the prosecution called 42 witnesses and presented 81 exhibits during the long trial.

What the judge said

The judge said she had looked at the points raised for the three men. These included that they had no earlier criminal record, their personal and health situations, and efforts to make peace with Sharon's family. But The Star reported she found that the seriousness of the crime outweighed these points.

Citizen Digital quoted the judge as saying Obado was "the architect of the criminal enterprise", meaning the person who planned it.

The court did not order the men to pay compensation to the family. According to The Star and Citizen Digital, the judge said there was not enough evidence of the family's losses to make such an order.

What the family asked for

Before the sentence, Sharon's parents told the court they wanted a non-custodial sentence for Obado, meaning he would not go to prison, so that he could keep supporting her children. NTV reported that her mother, Melinda Auma Rangili, said a death or life sentence would feel like another loss. The judge did not accept this request and chose prison.

The prosecution had argued for a strong sentence. NTV reported that state counsel Wangui Gichuhi told the court that murder is an offence against the State, not only against one family.

What happens next

The three men can appeal to the Court of Appeal under Kenyan law. None of the reports we read said whether they plan to do so, and their lawyers' reaction to the sentence was not reported.

The case has been followed closely across Kenya for eight years. It is one of the few cases in which a former governor has been convicted of murder.

Note: some reports spell Caspal Obiero's middle name differently (Ojwang or Ajwang), and describe his old job as county clerk or county employee.

stories.title: Sports roundup: Gor Mahia hit Mombasa United for three, Palace stun Real Sociedad, Osman shines for Brighton
key_points: Gor Mahia beat Mombasa United 3-0 at Nyayo and are now one point behind leaders KCB.
Reports say ex-Harambee Stars captain Victor Wanyama is set to take over Nairobi City Stars.
Crystal Palace came from behind to beat 10-man Real Sociedad 2-1 in the Europa League.
Ghana winger Ibrahim Osman scored twice as Brighton beat Universitatea Craiova, Flashscore reported.
stories.content:
Here is the top sports news from the last day, starting at home in Kenya.

FKF Premier League: Gor Mahia close the gap on KCB

Champions Gor Mahia beat bottom side Mombasa United 3-0 at Nyayo National Stadium in Nairobi on Thursday night, Mozzart Sport and Eastleigh Voice reported.

  • Ghanaian striker Ebenezer Assifuah scored first, in the 11th minute.
  • Shariff Musa added two more, in the 30th and 38th minutes, according to Mozzart Sport.

The win takes coach Charles Akonnor's side to 19 points, one point behind leaders KCB FC, and Gor have a game in hand. Gor moved above AFC Leopards into second place.

KCB stayed top after a big win over Murang'a Seal. Eastleigh Voice reported that KCB scored four goals. Mombasa United, who were promoted this season, remain bottom with two points from eight games before Thursday, Mozzart Sport said.

Wanyama linked with Nairobi City Stars takeover

Former Harambee Stars captain Victor Wanyama is set to take over troubled club Nairobi City Stars, K24 Digital reported on Friday. The deal has not been officially confirmed.

City Stars were relegated from the FKF Premier League at the end of the 2024/25 season and now play in the National Super League. K24 said the club did not travel to Homa Bay for a league match against MOFA FC on Tuesday, giving away a walkover. Wanyama and his brother McDonald Mariga are building a football academy in Nambale, Busia County.

Europa League: Palace fight back, Bournemouth stay perfect

Crystal Palace 2-1 Real Sociedad: Palace were losing at Selhurst Park after Mamadou Sarr scored for the Spanish side. Then Sociedad's Jon Martin was sent off for a second yellow card. Jean-Philippe Mateta equalised from the penalty spot, and Dwight McNeil scored the winner, Flashscore reported. It was Thomas Frank's first win as Palace manager.

Celta Vigo 1-2 Bournemouth: Bournemouth won in Spain despite playing most of the game with ten men, World Today Journal and Flashscore reported. Bournemouth are the only team in the league phase with five wins from five, World Today Journal said.

Other results: Sunderland drew 1-1 with Jagiellonia Białystok at the Stadium of Light, while Celtic won 2-1 away at Torreense in Portugal, according to Matrix News, which cited UK media reports.

Conference League: Osman stars for Brighton

Brighton beat Romania's Universitatea Craiova to stay unbeaten in the Conference League. Ghana winger Ibrahim Osman scored twice, according to Flashscore, which said Brighton moved to the top of the table.

What's next

The next Europa League matchday is on December 10, World Today Journal reported. Back home, FKF Premier League action continues this weekend.

stories.title: World roundup: Drone attack in Kuwait kills 2 Italians, Guinea-Bissau delays vote to 2028, Trump says he pressed Putin
key_points: Kuwait and Italy say an Iranian drone attack killed two Italian technicians in Kuwait; Iran denies any role.
Guinea-Bissau's military rulers moved elections from December 6 to November 2028.
Trump says he asked Putin to pull back military aggression across Europe and hopes for a quick Ukraine deal.
The Iran-related crisis keeps shipping in the Strait of Hormuz under threat, which affects fuel prices worldwide.
stories.content:
Here are the biggest world stories from the last 24 hours, in simple words.

1. Kuwait: drone attack kills two Italian workers

Two Italian technicians were killed on Thursday when drones hit a military air-defence station in Kuwait, according to Kuwait's defence ministry and Italy's foreign minister, Antonio Tajani. The two men worked for Rheinmetall Italia, a defence company. Tajani said two other people were injured: a Pakistani national and a Kuwaiti army captain.

Kuwait and Italy blamed Iran. Iran denied it. Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told his Kuwaiti and Italian counterparts that Iran had "no role or involvement whatsoever", The New Arab reported. Iran offered a joint investigation. The claims could not be independently confirmed.

The attack came as the war that began in February between Iran and the US and Israel continues to disrupt the Gulf. ABC News (Australia) reported that two more ships were hit in the Strait of Hormuz on the same day; the UK maritime agency UKMTO said both crews were safe.

Why it matters: many Kenyans work in Gulf countries such as Kuwait, Saudi Arabia and the UAE. Trouble around Hormuz also pushes up the cost of fuel and transport, including in Kenya.

2. Guinea-Bissau: military rulers delay elections by two years

Guinea-Bissau's military government has postponed presidential and parliamentary elections that were due on December 6. The new date is November 26, 2028, according to AP and RTÉ. Al Jazeera also reported the delay.

The decree was signed by transitional President General Horta Inta-a on Thursday, exactly one year after the army took power. It said the "technical, material and financial conditions" for a vote were not in place. The military seized power in November 2025, three days after an election, removing President Umaro Sissoco Embaló before results were announced. The West African bloc ECOWAS had asked for a short transition, Al Jazeera said.

Why it matters: it is one more West African country where soldiers are staying in power longer than promised.

3. Trump says he asked Putin to "pull back" in Europe

US President Donald Trump said on Thursday that he asked Russian President Vladimir Putin to pull back military aggression against territories across Europe. They met last week in Shenzhen, China, at the APEC leaders' meeting, Reuters reported.

Writing on Truth Social, Trump said he hopes Russia and Ukraine can make a deal soon. "I really believe this is a strong possibility," he wrote. He also said the biggest obstacle is the deep dislike between Putin and Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky. There are no formal peace talks at the moment, according to the Reuters report.

The Kremlin said no decision has been made on whether Putin will attend the G20 summit in Florida on December 14–15.

4. EU leaders argue over the next long-term budget

European Union leaders met on Thursday to discuss the bloc's budget for 2028 to 2034, worth nearly €1.6 trillion, and money for Ukraine, The Standard (Hong Kong) reported. No final deal was reported.

Why it matters: the EU is one of Kenya's biggest trade and aid partners, so its budget choices affect support for Africa.

5. US: Thanksgiving storm cuts power on the East Coast

A strong storm hit the US East Coast on Thanksgiving Day, with wind gusts of up to 70 mph (112 km/h), The Standard (Hong Kong) reported. Falling trees and power lines left hundreds of thousands of customers without electricity, and flights were disrupted.

Why it matters: Kenyans in the US travelling this holiday weekend should check their flight status and local power updates before leaving home.

stories.title: Green card in immigration court? New US ruling says your medical exam must be done before approval
key_points: The US Board of Immigration Appeals ruled on November 24 that a judge cannot grant a green card on a promise to send the medical exam later.
The ruling is mainly for people asking for a green card in immigration court, including people in detention.
Simple step: make sure your completed Form I-693 medical exam is in the file before your hearing.
Also: Senator Edwin Sifuna's US tour reaches Dallas today and Houston on Sunday.
stories.content:
A new decision by a top US immigration body affects Kenyans and other immigrants who are asking for a green card (permanent residence) in immigration court. In short: the medical exam must be finished and in the file before the judge approves the green card.

What was decided

The Board of Immigration Appeals (BIA) is the highest immigration appeals body in the US Justice Department. On November 24 it published a decision called Matter of Aguilar Ceballos, according to Immigration Analytics and GSM Global News.

The Board said an immigration judge may not approve a green card on the condition that the applicant sends the medical exam form (Form I-693) later. Immigration Analytics quoted the Board as saying such a conditional grant is "improper".

The case involved a man from Mexico. In December 2025 a judge gave him a green card and allowed him 60 days to send his medical exam. The government appealed. He did the exam in January 2026, but the Board still sent the case back to the judge so the exam and updated background checks can be properly added to the record.

Who it affects

  • Mainly people in immigration court (removal proceedings) who are asking a judge for a green card. This includes people in detention, who can find it harder to see an approved doctor.
  • The decision is binding on immigration judges and on government lawyers in those cases, Immigration Analytics said.
  • It does not undo green cards that became final before.

Some reports, including Mwakilishi, described the ruling as covering every family and job-based green card application. Specialist sources say the ruling itself is about immigration court. For applications filed with USCIS (the agency that handles most green cards), Immigration Analytics notes that USCIS has already required the medical form to be sent together with Form I-485 since December 2, 2024.

What you can do now

  • If you have a green card case in immigration court, check with your lawyer that a completed, signed Form I-693 is in the record before your final hearing.
  • Only a USCIS-approved doctor (called a civil surgeon) can do the exam.
  • If the exam is not ready, Immigration Analytics says the better step is to ask the judge for a short delay (a continuance), not a conditional approval.
  • This is general information, not legal advice. Speak to a licensed immigration lawyer about your own case.

Also for Kenyans in the US

Sifuna tour in Texas: Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna's Linda Mwananchi tour moves to Texas. According to the schedule published by Capital FM, there is a Thanksgiving dinner in Dallas today, November 27, and a women's meeting and town hall in Houston on Sunday, November 29. The tour then goes to the Seattle area (December 3–4) and California (December 5–7).

Search in Alabama: Mwakilishi reported that a 23-year-old Kenyan, John O. Anyiko of Birmingham, went missing on Logan Martin Lake in Talladega County early on Saturday, November 21. As of Wednesday, state and local teams led by the Alabama Law Enforcement Agency were still searching, the outlet said, and no recovery had been announced.

stories.title: High Court says government broke the Constitution over US-backed Ebola centre in Laikipia, orders deals made public
key_points: The High Court ruled on Thursday that the government did not involve or inform Laikipia residents about a US-backed Ebola quarantine centre.
The Ministry of Health has 45 days to make the agreements and assessments public.
No more building or use of the centre at Laikipia Air Base until the court is satisfied.
Also: DAP-K leader Eugene Wamalwa drops Governor George Natembeya and Ayub Savula as deputy party leaders.
stories.content:
The High Court in Kenya has ruled that the government broke the Constitution when it allowed a US-backed Ebola quarantine centre to be set up in Laikipia County without involving local people. The judgment was delivered on Thursday, November 26.

What the court decided

The court found that the government did not properly inform residents or let them take part in decisions about the centre at Laikipia Air Base, a military base. The Star reported that the judge said this went against Article 10 of the Constitution (national values, including public participation) and Article 35 (the right to information).

The court gave two main orders, according to The Star and the Associated Press (AP):

  • 45 days: the Ministry of Health must make the documents public. The Star says these include the agreements, health and environment assessments, approvals and operating rules. AP says the government must disclose all agreements with the United States.
  • Work stops: no more construction or use of the centre until the court confirms the government has obeyed.

"Constitutional accountability is not satisfied by asking citizens to trust that all is well," the judge said, as quoted by The Star.

The Star reported that the judge made clear the case was not against Kenya's cooperation with the US, or against the Health Ministry's role. It was about how the decision was made. (The Star and AP gave different names for the judge, so we have left the name out.)

Who went to court, and why

The case was brought by the Katiba Institute, a constitutional rights group. AP says the Law Society of Kenya (LSK) was also a petitioner. The petitioners argued that the centre put the rights to life, health and information at risk, and that Kenya's health system was not ready for an Ebola outbreak.

AP reported that the centre has 50 beds, and that it led to deadly protests by residents who feared they could be exposed to the disease. In May, the High Court had already ordered a halt to construction while the case was heard.

The US link

According to AP, officials in the Trump administration had said Americans exposed to Ebola abroad would be sent to the centre. The US also planned to give Kenya $13.5 million to prepare for Ebola.

AP said Kenya recorded its first Ebola case in October, in a Kenyan who had travelled from Congo through Uganda. Kenya has since recorded nine cases, all close contacts of the first patient, AP said.

The government had not given a public reply to the ruling in the reports we saw. In October, Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale said the government was waiting for the court's direction on the centre, AP reported.

Also in Kenya politics: shake-up in DAP-K

Eugene Wamalwa, leader of the Democratic Action Party of Kenya (DAP-K), announced on Thursday that Trans Nzoia Governor George Natembeya and Kakamega Deputy Governor Ayub Savula are no longer the party's deputy leaders, Citizen Digital and The Standard reported.

Mumias East MP Peter Salasya and former Cabinet minister Kipruto arap Kirwa are set to take the posts. Nairobi Wire reported that the party's National Executive Council still has to approve the change next week.

Natembeya has been working with Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna's Linda Mwananchi movement, which named him to head its presidential campaign. Savula joined President William Ruto's UDA party earlier this year, The Standard reported. Tusker beat Posta Rangers 2-1 in the FKF Premier League; Nairobi City Thunder lost at home in the Road to BAL.
Liverpool won 3-0 at Club Brugge; Manchester United drew 2-2 at Sporting.

stories.content:
Here is the top sports news of the last two days, starting at home.

FKF and Red Cross sign KSh54m medical deal

The Football Kenya Federation (FKF) and the Kenya Red Cross Society signed a KSh54 million partnership in Nairobi on Tuesday, November 24, Citizen Digital and other outlets reported. The deal provides ambulances, first aid, training for medical staff and equipment such as stretchers at matches in the FKF Premier League, the Women's Premier League, the National Super League and the Women's National Super League, plus international games. Division One gets first aid.

FKF president Hussein Mohammed also challenged the national team to reach the 2030 World Cup. "Kenya must qualify for World Cup 2030," he said, according to Citizen Digital. Kenya has never played at a World Cup finals.

FKF Premier League: Tusker beat Posta Rangers

Tusker beat Posta Rangers 2-1 on Wednesday at St Sebastian Park in Murang'a, Mozzart Sport and 365Scores reported. Chrisphine Erambo and Victor Mbaoma scored for Tusker before Mark Shaban pulled one back late for Posta. Mozzart Sport says it was Tusker's third win of the season.

In other games reported by Mozzart Sport, 10-man APS Bomet drew 0-0 with Migori Youth, and Nairobi United beat 3K FC 2-0.

Basketball: Thunder lose at home

Kenyan champions Nairobi City Thunder lost 83-71 to Zambia's Munali Suns at Kasarani on Tuesday in the Road to BAL Elite 16, Capital FM and Citizen Digital reported. The score was 37-37 at half-time before the Suns pulled away. Tylor Ongwae led Thunder with 21 points. Thunder face South Sudan's Patriots BC on Thursday night.

Champions League: Liverpool cruise, United held

In Wednesday's Champions League games:

  • Club Brugge 0-3 Liverpool: Alexander Isak scored twice and Florian Wirtz once. Liverpool now have 12 points from five games.
  • Sporting 2-2 Manchester United: Bruno Fernandes scored twice soon after half-time, once from the penalty spot, but Sporting's Luis Suarez also scored twice. United's Youri Tielemans was sent off late. New coach Mauricio Pochettino is still waiting for his first win.
  • Lille 2-1 Bayern Munich: Dayot Upamecano put Bayern ahead, but Ayase Ueda and an own goal turned it around. It was Bayern's first defeat of the season.
  • PSG 2-2 Roma: A late Donyell Malen penalty ended PSG's run of four wins from four in the league phase.
  • Sabah 1-4 Barcelona: Anthony Gordon scored twice.
  • Also: Inter 2-0 Stuttgart, Atletico Madrid 2-0 Viking, Shakhtar 0-1 Fenerbahce, Slavia Prague 0-1 Villarreal.

Ivory Coast winger Amad Diallo had a goal ruled out for Manchester United in Lisbon.

Coming up

Kenya's sevens team, Shujaa, plays at the Dubai tournament from November 27 to 29, according to Citizen Digital. The CAF Champions League group stage also starts this weekend.

stories.title: World roundup: Houthi-Saudi fighting spreads to ports, Ukraine strike in Libya kills 2, Cairo tanker fire kills 31
key_points: Houthi rebels and the Saudi-led coalition traded strikes on ports and oil sites; Iran says 2 more tankers hit mines.
Two Libyan officers died after a Ukrainian drone attack on a Russian warship in Benghazi.
Drone strikes in Sudan's Blue Nile state killed about 19 civilians, rights groups say.
A fuel tanker fire on a Cairo highway killed at least 31 people; the US proposed new tariffs on 14 economies.
stories.content:
Here are the biggest world stories of the last 24 hours, and what they mean for Kenyans and Africans.

1. Houthi-Saudi fighting spreads to ports and oil sites

Fighting between Yemen's Houthi rebels and the Saudi-led coalition grew this week. On Tuesday a Houthi drone hit a tower in Riyadh's financial district. Saudi authorities said 11 people were hurt. The coalition then struck Hodeidah port in Yemen, which, according to the UN, handles most of Yemen's aid. No casualty figures were given.

On Wednesday the Houthis said they hit Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura oil refinery. The coalition said it shot down four drones there and did not confirm any hit. The Houthis also told workers at Saudi Red Sea ports, including Jeddah, to leave. Early Thursday the coalition said it stopped two missiles aimed at Riyadh, Anadolu reported.

Separately, Iran's Revolutionary Guard said two more oil tankers hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday. The ships were not named and the claim has not been independently confirmed.

Why it matters: Many Kenyans live and work in Saudi Arabia and the Gulf. Higher oil prices also push up fuel costs at home.

2. Ukraine's war reaches Libya

Two officers of Khalifa Haftar's Libyan National Army died on Tuesday of wounds from a Ukrainian sea-drone attack on a Russian warship in Benghazi on Sunday, AP and Al Jazeera reported. Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy confirmed the attack. Kyiv says the ship was sunk; Libyan officials told AP it was badly damaged. The Libyan army has vowed to respond. Ukraine said it did not target Libyans.

Why it matters: Analysts say the attack could disrupt Russia's supply route to its forces in the Sahel, pulling Africa deeper into a war far away.

3. Sudan: drone strikes kill civilians in Blue Nile

Night drone strikes on homes in Damazin, capital of Sudan's Blue Nile state, killed 19 civilians on Tuesday, according to the rights group Emergency Lawyers. The Sudan Doctors Network gave a toll of 17. Both groups blamed the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF), which did not respond to Reuters. Blue Nile borders South Sudan and Ethiopia.

Why it matters: Fighting near East Africa's borders raises the risk of more people fleeing to neighbouring countries.

4. Egypt: tanker fire on Cairo highway kills 31

A fuel tanker crashed and caught fire on the Ring Road in Giza, part of Greater Cairo, on Wednesday evening. Egypt's Health Ministry said at least 31 people died and 21 were injured. More than two dozen vehicles burned. The cause has not been confirmed.

5. US proposes new tariffs on 14 economies

The US Trade Representative proposed new import taxes on 14 trading partners, including China, the European Union, India and Vietnam. Trade chief Jamieson Greer said most rates would be 15 to 20 percent and nothing would start for at least a couple of months, according to reports quoting CNBC. Public hearings start in January. No African country is on the list. Asian stock markets fell on the news.

Why it matters: Some of Kenya's competitors in selling clothes to the US are on the list, while Kenya is not.

stories.title: Sifuna answers critics of his US tour as filings show diaspora fundraising plan; Dallas is next
key_points: Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna told Kenyans in Maryland he will not stay away from the US because there are 'no votes here'.
US filings show a plan to raise money from Kenyans in North America for his movement, Kenyan media report.
The tour moves to Dallas for a Thanksgiving dinner on November 27, then Houston, Seattle and California.
Visiting the US Embassy in Nairobi? It is closed for visa and consular services on November 26 (Thanksgiving).
stories.content:
Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna has told Kenyans in the United States that their views matter, even though few of them vote. He spoke in Maryland, one stop on a US tour that has now passed through New Jersey, Pennsylvania and the Washington, DC area. Sifuna plans to run for president in 2027.

What he said in Maryland

The Star and Mwakilishi both reported that Sifuna answered people who say politicians should not spend time in the diaspora because Kenyans abroad cast few votes.

"I don't want to be told not to come to the US on the reason that there are no votes here," he said, according to both outlets.

He also rejected advice that he should be "nicer" to win the presidency. He said the rules of his party, ODM, and of the Linda Mwananchi Movement he now leads, expect leaders to speak out against wrongdoing. The reports did not name the exact venue or date of the Maryland meeting.

What the US filings show

The Nation reported this week that US filings describe a plan to raise money from Kenyans abroad for Sifuna's campaign. Mwakilishi carried the same report.

According to Streamline Feed, which cites Tuko, the papers were filed with the US Department of Justice on October 28 under the Foreign Agents Registration Act (FARA). This US law asks people who do political work in America for a foreign politician or party to register and say what they do. Filing is a legal requirement, not a sign of wrongdoing.

Streamline Feed says the filing names Gilbert Shanga, a Kenyan based in Hackettstown, New Jersey, as coordinator. His listed tasks include arranging political meetings, encouraging fundraising among Kenyans in North America and meeting US officials. No amounts of money have been reported. These details come from one outlet and KASS-mtv could not check the filing itself. Sifuna's team has not commented publicly on the reports.

Background: according to Streamline Feed, Sifuna took over The Equitable Party in October, and delegates voted on November 13 to rename it the Linda Mwananchi Movement.

Where the tour goes next

Capital FM published this schedule for the rest of the tour:

  • November 27, Dallas: Thanksgiving dinner at the Mar Thoma Event Center.
  • November 29, Houston: women's meeting and a town hall.
  • December 3–4, Seattle area: Federal Way and Renton.
  • December 5, San Francisco Bay Area: town hall and gala in Oakland.
  • December 7, Silicon Valley: closing dinner.

Plans can change, so check with local organisers before you travel.

Why it matters

More politicians are visiting the US ahead of the 2027 election. For Kenyans in America, these meetings are a chance to ask questions about issues that affect them directly, such as consular services, the cost of sending money home and whether diaspora voting will be expanded.

Quick travel note

According to Mwakilishi, the US Embassy in Nairobi has suspended visa and consular services on Thursday, November 26, for the US Thanksgiving holiday. If you or your family have an appointment, check the embassy's website for the new date.

stories.title: Opposition boycotts IEBC meeting, gives commission until December and threatens protests from January
key_points: Opposition leaders stayed away from an IEBC meeting with political parties on Wednesday, November 25.
They say the IEBC has until December to act on their demands, or they will lead protests from January.
The meeting went ahead. Other party leaders criticised Gachagua's 'briefcase parties' remark.
Separately, the IEBC said it has not cleared Gachagua to run for president in 2027.
stories.content:
Kenya's main opposition leaders boycotted a meeting called by the electoral commission (IEBC) on Wednesday, November 25. They said they will lead countrywide protests from January if the commission does not meet their demands by December.

Instead of attending, the leaders held a joint press briefing in Nairobi. The IEBC meeting went ahead with other political parties.

Who was there

The Star and Mwakilishi report that the briefing brought together former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua (DCP leader), former Chief Justice David Maraga (United Green Movement), former Attorney General Justin Muturi (Democratic Party), Martha Karua (People's Liberation Party), Fred Matiang'i (Jubilee), Jimmy Wanjigi (Safina) and Kiharu MP Ndindi Nyoro.

According to Citizen Digital, this was the second time the opposition has stayed away from IEBC talks. On November 19 some of them walked out of an earlier meeting.

Why they stayed away

Gachagua said the meeting was organised by the State Department for Interior, not the IEBC alone, and asked why President William Ruto was speaking for the commission. He called the parties that attended "briefcase parties". "We are not willing to engage in a charade," he said, according to Citizen Digital.

Maraga said attending would only approve decisions that were already made. He said the IEBC is "captured", a claim the commission has not accepted.

What they want

The Star reports that the opposition's demands include:

  • an independent audit of the voter register to remove dead and double-registered voters;
  • open election technology that can be checked independently;
  • results sent electronically from polling stations and shown live, with a public results website;
  • scrapping the National Tallying Centre;
  • hiring returning officers on merit.

The Star says the IEBC has until December to respond. If it does not, the leaders say they will mobilise Kenyans from January to take their complaints to IEBC offices across the country. Kenyans.co.ke reported Gachagua's timeline a little differently, saying action could start "next month". Kenyans.co.ke also reported that Maraga called for voter registration desks in US states with many Kenyans.

The other side

Citizen Digital reports that the IEBC briefed the parties that attended on voter registration, the voter register audit and buying election technology. IEBC Chairperson Erastus Edung Ethekon said the commission will follow court directions on the national tallying centre and treat all parties equally.

Leaders of parties that attended rejected Gachagua's words. Evans Misati, chair of the Political Parties Liaison Committee, said DCP is one of 105 registered parties and will get no special treatment. Ford Kenya chairman Joel Ruhu said: "We are political parties just like the rest."

President Ruto has warned politicians against threatening the IEBC or organising protests against it, according to The Star and Citizen Digital.

IEBC: Gachagua not yet cleared

Also on Wednesday, the IEBC said it "has neither cleared nor made any determination" on whether Gachagua can run for president. This came after its legal director, Chrispine Owiye, told journalists on Tuesday that leaders whose removal is under appeal are not automatically barred.

The commission said a presidential candidate's eligibility will be decided at the nomination stage, which has not started. Gachagua was impeached in October 2024. The High Court upheld his removal in June 2026, and his appeal is still pending. No response from Gachagua to the IEBC statement had been reported.

Kenya's next general election is due in August 2027.

The Sisibo Marathon on December 19 offers Ksh25 million in prizes, Ksh5 million for each winner, organisers say.

stories.content:
Here is the top sports news of the last two days, starting at home in Kenya.

Kipchoge: Kenya should host a marathon major

Marathon great Eliud Kipchoge says Kenya should aim to host one of the World Marathon Majors, the group of the biggest city marathons such as London, Berlin and New York. He spoke on Sunday at the launch of the new Sisibo Marathon in Eldoret, The Standard reported.

Kipchoge said he hopes the Sisibo race can become Africa's first World Marathon Major in 2027. That is his hope; no official bid decision has been reported. He also called for a Diamond League athletics meeting in Kenya. Athletics Kenya president Jackson Tuwei supported bringing more global events to Kenya and also spoke about the fight against doping.

Olympic 1500m champion Faith Kipyegon and New York City Marathon champion Sheila Chepkirui were among the stars at the launch.

Sisibo Marathon: big prize money

The first Sisibo Marathon will be run in Eldoret on December 19, 2026, according to Uasin Gishu News. Athletics Kenya official Barnaba Korir announced total prize money of Ksh25 million. The men's and women's winners will each get Ksh5 million, second place Ksh3 million and third place Ksh1 million. Organisers say it will be the richest race in Kenya and Africa, and that entry will be free and open to all.

Why it matters: Big races at home give Kenyan runners a chance to earn well without travelling abroad, and can bring visitors and money to the North Rift.

Champions League: Real Madrid strong, English clubs held

Tuesday night was matchday five of the Champions League league phase. Results, from AFP and France 24 reports:

  • Real Madrid 5-1 PSV Eindhoven: PSV led at half-time through an Ivan Perisic penalty. Madrid hit back with goals from Federico Valverde, Jude Bellingham, two from Kylian Mbappe and one from Vinicius Junior. Madrid have won all five games and have 15 points.
  • Arsenal 1-1 Borussia Dortmund: Viktor Gyokeres scored early for Arsenal, but Maximilian Beier levelled after the break.

  • Galatasaray 1-0 Aston Villa: a late Deniz Gul header beat Villa, who stay on nine points.
  • Other results: Como 1-0 AEK Athens, Slovan Bratislava 0-2 Real Betis, RB Leipzig 3-1 Lens, Bodo/Glimt 1-0 LASK.

On Wednesday, Paris Saint-Germain host Roma. A PSG win would take them level with Real Madrid on 15 points.

Coming up

In the Premier League this weekend, the big game is Arsenal against Manchester City on Sunday. At home, the row between Harambee Stars coach Benni McCarthy and the Football Kenya Federation over team preparations is still being watched closely by fans.

stories.title: World roundup: Israeli strike kills Hamas security chief, Russia hits Zaporizhzhia, Amnesty raises Tigray war crimes concern
key_points: Israeli strikes in Gaza killed a senior Hamas security official and others on Tuesday, Reuters reported.
A Russian attack on an apartment building in Zaporizhzhia, Ukraine, killed 2 people, a Ukrainian official said.
Amnesty International says Ethiopian shelling of towns in Tigray should be investigated as possible war crimes.
Bangladesh's former leader Sheikh Hasina plans to return on December 16; the government says she will be arrested.
stories.content:
Here are the biggest world stories of the last day, in short and simple form. Most details come from Reuters reports, as summarised by the US website Just Security.

1. Gaza: Israeli strikes kill Hamas security chief

Israeli airstrikes on Tuesday killed Naeem Abu Nahel, described as the head of Hamas's internal security service in Gaza, and six other people, Reuters reported, citing medics and police. One strike hit western Gaza City. Others hit areas near Khan Younis and the Netzarim corridor.

The Israeli military and the Shin Bet security service said they struck a senior Hamas militant. The Hamas-run interior ministry said two of the dead were police officers. These claims have not been independently checked.

Why it matters: Each new strike puts more strain on the fragile Gaza truce and on aid for people living in tents during winter.

2. Ukraine: Russian strike hits apartment block in Zaporizhzhia

An overnight Russian attack hit an apartment building in the city of Zaporizhzhia, killing two people, Reuters reported. Regional governor Mykhailo Semikin said dozens were wounded, including children. Early reports gave different numbers for the wounded, so the final count is not yet clear.

Why it matters: The attacks go on while efforts at peace talks continue. The war still affects global food and fuel prices.

3. Ethiopia: Amnesty calls for war crimes probe in Tigray

Rights group Amnesty International said artillery strikes on towns in northern Tigray this year by Ethiopian forces and allied militia should be investigated as possible war crimes, Reuters reported. Amnesty also accused the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) of putting civilians at risk during the September battle for the town of Alamata, by placing fighters in homes and using schools. These are Amnesty's findings; Ethiopia's response was not included in the reports we saw.

Why it matters: Ethiopia is Kenya's neighbour. New fighting in Tigray could affect refugees, trade and peace in the Horn of Africa.

4. Bangladesh: Hasina says she will return on December 16

Former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina plans to go back to Bangladesh on December 16, her spokesperson told Reuters. She has lived in India since she was removed from power in 2024. A Bangladeshi court sentenced her to death in her absence last year over the deadly crackdown on the 2024 protests. Foreign Minister Humayun Kabir said she would not return on her own terms and would be brought back in handcuffs, the BBC reported.

5. US: doubt over end of military aid to Israel

The US ambassador to Israel, Mike Huckabee, said he is not sure that about $3.8 billion a year in US military aid to Israel will end by the end of 2026, as President Donald Trump said on November 3, Reuters reported. Huckabee said the aid is meant to continue for two more years.

Why it matters: US decisions on foreign aid, from military help to health funding, affect many countries, including Kenya.

stories.title: eCitizen hack claim: what Kenyans in the US should do now to protect their accounts
key_points: Hackers claim they stole about 740GB of data from Kenya's eCitizen portal. The government has not confirmed any data loss.
The State Department for Immigration and Citizen Services says it is investigating and eCitizen still works as usual.
Users are told to change their password, use a strong one, and never share their password or OTP code.
Kenyans abroad use eCitizen for passports and other services, so this matters to the diaspora.
stories.content:
The Kenyan government is investigating claims that hackers broke into eCitizen, the website Kenyans use for most government services. It has asked users to change their passwords. For Kenyans in the United States, who use eCitizen for passports and many other services, this is a good time to check your account.

What happened

On Tuesday, November 24, the State Department for Immigration and Citizen Services said it was aware of reports of a possible hack and was investigating. This office is part of the Ministry of Interior, led by Cabinet Secretary Kipchumba Murkomen.

The office said it is checking how far any damage went and whether any data reached the wrong people. It said "eCitizen services remain available" and people can keep using government services as usual. It promised updates after its technical investigation.

What the hackers claim

A group calling itself "ByteToBreach" claims it took about 740GB of data, according to Mwakilishi, which cited a cyber security monitoring firm called VECERT Analyser. The group claims this includes:

  • about 600GB of personal identity and verification documents;
  • about 100GB of government database records;
  • about 40GB of computer code.

Reports also say the attackers claim they reached systems linked to the Social Health Authority (SHA), the DCI and the National Police Service. None of these claims has been confirmed. The government has not confirmed a breach, the amount of data, or that any data was lost.

What you should do now: step by step

  • Step 1: Log in to eCitizen only by typing the official address yourself. Do not click links in texts or emails.
  • Step 2: Change your eCitizen password. Choose a long, strong password you do not use anywhere else.
  • Step 3: If you used the same password for email, banking or M-Pesa, change those passwords too.
  • Step 4: Never share your password or one-time PIN (OTP). The government says eCitizen will never ask you for them.
  • Step 5: Be careful with calls, WhatsApp messages or emails that say they are from eCitizen, the embassy or immigration. Scammers often use news like this to trick people.
  • Step 6: Check your account for anything strange, such as applications or payments you did not make, and report it through official channels.

Why this matters for the diaspora

Kenyans abroad depend on eCitizen for passport applications and renewals, ID and civil registration services, and paying government fees. Many of them upload copies of passports, IDs and birth certificates. That is why the claim of stolen identity documents worries many people abroad, even though it is not yet confirmed.

If you have a passport or other application in progress, the government says services are still running. Keep watching official government and embassy channels for updates, and avoid sharing unverified posts.

Also this week

Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna's Linda Mwananchi Movement tour of the US continues in the Maryland and Washington DC area this week. Next is a Thanksgiving dinner in Dallas on November 27, then Houston on November 29, according to the tour schedule reported by Capital FM.

stories.title: Kenya and DR Congo agree to bring back ambassadors after Ruto-Tshisekedi talks in Oyo
key_points: Ruto and DR Congo's President Tshisekedi met in Oyo, Republic of the Congo, on Sunday, November 22.
They agreed to work towards full diplomatic ties, including the return of ambassadors. No date has been given.
The two countries have had no ambassadors in each other's capitals for years, after a row over the M23-linked AFC alliance launched in Nairobi in December 2023.
At home on Tuesday, Ruto said the Hustler Fund will get Ksh5 billion more and some borrowing limits will rise.
stories.content:
Kenya and the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) have agreed to repair their broken relationship. President William Ruto and DRC President Felix Tshisekedi met on Sunday, November 22, in Oyo, a town in the Republic of the Congo. They agreed to work towards full diplomatic ties, including bringing back ambassadors.

Who brought them together

The talks were hosted by Republic of the Congo President Denis Sassou N'Guesso. Togo's leader, Faure Gnassingbé, who is the African Union's mediator for eastern DRC, helped lead the talks. Ruto cut short his tour of Western Kenya to travel to Oyo, Dawan Africa and Xinhua reported.

What went wrong between the two countries

The trouble started in December 2023. A new political and military alliance, the Congo River Alliance (AFC), was launched in Nairobi. The AFC is linked to the M23 rebels who fight the Congolese army in eastern DRC. Kinshasa was angry and recalled its ambassador from Kenya, according to Xinhua and Uganda's The Independent.

Relations got worse after that. In January 2025, rioters in Kinshasa attacked and looted the Kenyan embassy, Kenyans.co.ke reported. The DRC also did not accept Kenya's chosen ambassador, Peter Tum. In October 2025, Nairobi hosted Congolese opposition figures, including former president Joseph Kabila. Kenya said it could not stop people from expressing political views.

What they agreed

According to a joint statement reported by several outlets, the two leaders agreed to:

  • work towards full diplomatic relations, including the return of ambassadors;
  • restart their Joint Grand Commission for Cooperation and hold regular talks;
  • solve differences through dialogue and respect each other's borders and independence;
  • grow trade, investment and security cooperation;
  • work together on stopping Ebola.

Ruto said the two countries had agreed to "open a new chapter", Dawan Africa reported. The DRC presidency said on X that the leaders agreed to fully restore relations, notably through the return of their ambassadors, according to Xinhua.

Outlets used slightly different words. Citizen Digital said the leaders agreed to "work towards" restoring ambassadors, while Xinhua said they agreed to "fully restore" ties. No outlet has reported a date for the ambassadors to return. Kenya's foreign ministry has not given further details in the reports we saw.

Why it matters

The DRC is a big trade partner for Kenya and a member of the East African Community (EAC). Many Kenyan traders, truck drivers and businesses work in eastern DRC. Better ties could make trade and travel easier. The two countries also share the fight against Ebola in the region.

Also in Kenya politics on Tuesday

Hustler Fund: Speaking at State House, Nairobi, at a Joyful Women Organisation (JOYWO) event, Ruto said the government will add Ksh5 billion to the Hustler Fund. He said more than 4.5 million borrowers will move to a bridge loan of up to Ksh150,000, and those stuck at a Ksh10,000 limit will get higher limits if they repay, Kenyans.co.ke reported.

Malala stays with DCP: Cleophas Malala, deputy leader of Rigathi Gachagua's DCP party, denied reports that he has joined Senator Edwin Sifuna's Linda Mwananchi Movement or is running for Nairobi governor. He said he is still running for Kakamega governor on a DCP ticket, according to Kenyans.co.ke.

stories.content:
Here are the biggest world stories of the last day, in short and simple form.

1. Iran says three tankers hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy said late on Monday that three oil tankers struck mines in the Strait of Hormuz and caught fire, Anadolu Agency reported. The IRGC also said US air cover did not stop the incidents, and warned ships not to use what it calls "unauthorized routes."

These are Iran's claims and have not been independently confirmed. Iran closed the strait in July after US strikes resumed, and it has reported similar tanker fires several times since October, Al Jazeera and other outlets reported.

Why it matters for Kenya: a large share of the world's oil passes through this strait. Trouble there can push up fuel prices, including in Kenya.

2. Gaza: drone strike and winter floods

An Israeli drone strike killed three Palestinians and wounded five at a police post in Al-Mawasi, Khan Younis, early on Tuesday, a medical source at Nasser Hospital said, according to Anadolu. Gaza's Health Ministry says 1,675 Palestinians have been killed since the ceasefire began on October 10, 2025.

US Senator Brian Schatz has asked Israel to let in winter supplies and building materials after heavy rain flooded more than 70,000 tents. Israel's aid agency, COGAT, has said it delivered tens of thousands of tents before the storms, Latin Times reported.

3. Russia and Ukraine clash at the UN

At the UN Security Council on Monday, Russia ruled out bringing back a Black Sea grain deal. It accused Ukraine of attacking more than 200 commercial ships since July, Anadolu reported. Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned of new Russian strikes and asked allies for more Patriot air-defence missiles.

The President of the European Commission announced a new package of sanctions on Russia. It targets banks and crypto platforms and Russia's role in European sports and cultural events.

Why it matters for Africa: the Black Sea is a major route for wheat and fertiliser bought by African countries.

4. Nvidia brings back its CEO

Nvidia, the world's leading maker of AI chips, has reinstated Jensen Huang as president and chief executive. The company said talks with senior US officials led its board to decide his return poses no national security risk, Anadolu reported.

5. Also today

  • South Korea sent fighter jets after Russian military planes entered its air defence zone, Yonhap reported.
  • Libya's leaders warned that the country risks being dragged into the Russia–Ukraine and Sudan conflicts.
  • Zambia and Türkiye agreed to work together on water projects, investment and climate resilience.

stories.title: Sifuna's US tour moves to Maryland and DC after packed Allentown town hall
key_points: The Allentown, Pennsylvania town hall on Sunday was filled to capacity, Mwakilishi and K24 reported.

Today (Nov 24) he has a policy meeting and a luncheon with Maryland elected officials; Wednesday ends with a town hall.

stories.content:
WASHINGTON, DC — Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna's tour of the United States has reached Maryland and the Washington DC area, after a busy first weekend in New Jersey and Pennsylvania.

Sifuna leads the Linda Mwananchi Movement (LMM) and wants to run for president in Kenya's August 2027 election. His trip runs from November 21 to December 7, according to Mwakilishi, a news site for Kenyans in the US.

What happened at the weekend

In our Sunday story, we promised to report what happened at the Allentown town hall. Here it is.

  • New Jersey: supporters met him at Newark airport with songs, dances and banners. He opened the movement's first office outside Kenya, in Hackettstown, New Jersey. Mwakilishi said the office will run volunteer work, voter outreach and fundraising on the East Coast.
  • Pennsylvania: on Sunday, November 22, he went to a morning service at Grace Community Church in Allentown. In the afternoon, he spoke at a town hall at The Palace Center. Mwakilishi said the hall was full, with Kenyans from Pennsylvania, New York and New Jersey. K24 Digital said a video Sifuna shared showed every seat taken.

At the town hall, Sifuna answered critics who had doubted his support in the region. He talked about governance, economic accountability and the constitution, Mwakilishi reported.

This week in Maryland and DC

  • Monday, Nov 23: business community dinner in Maryland.
  • Today, Tuesday, Nov 24: an East Africa politics and policy meeting, then a luncheon with Afri Thrive and Maryland elected officials.
  • Wednesday, Nov 25: a brunch with women from the DC area, a talk with the 6.25 Movement and Gen Z Movement, and an evening town hall.

The rest of the tour

  • Texas: Thanksgiving dinner with families in Dallas on November 27; women's meeting and town hall in Houston on November 29.
  • Washington State: December 3–4, church service in Federal Way and a gala dinner in Renton.
  • California: December 5, town hall in San Francisco and a gala in Oakland; December 7, closing dinner with Kenyan professionals in Silicon Valley.

Dates and venues can change, so check with local organisers before you travel.

Why it matters

Kenyans abroad send home billions of shillings every year. But very few vote: fewer than 600 Kenyans living in the US were registered to vote in 2022, Mwakilishi reported. Analysts say tours like this one matter mostly for raising campaign money and shaping debate at home.

Back in Kenya, the opposition is asking the electoral commission to allow electronic voting for Kenyans abroad. That could change how much the diaspora vote counts in the future.

Other leaders, including Rigathi Gachagua and David Maraga, have made similar trips to the US. The Nation noted that these tours include a large fundraising part.

stories.title: IEBC's Smartmatic deal ends today as opposition sets January deadline and 94 parties are told to fix nomination rules
key_points: The IEBC's 2021 support contract with Smartmatic, its election technology supplier, ends today, November 24.
Gachagua has given the IEBC until January to answer opposition demands, or face nationwide protests.
The IEBC says court cases have slowed its buying of new election technology.
Only 11 of 105 parties passed the IEBC's first check of nomination rules; 94, including UDA and ODM, must fix theirs.
stories.content:
NAIROBI — Kenya's election body, the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC), reaches an important date today, Tuesday, November 24. Its support contract with Smartmatic, the company that supplies its election technology, ends today, according to People Daily and the Nation.

Smartmatic's equipment and systems were used in the 2022 General Election. The next General Election is on August 10, 2027.

Why the date matters

The IEBC uses this technology to register voters and identify them. People Daily said the end of the contract raises questions about technical support, software licences and security updates.

Opposition leader Rigathi Gachagua, the former Deputy President who now leads the Democracy for the Citizens Party (DCP), has warned that a new system could take five to six months to buy. He says this could disrupt voter registration, Capital FM reported.

The IEBC has not said publicly what will happen after today. The Nation reported that the High Court has certified as urgent a case that seeks to stop the IEBC from giving a Sh17.6 billion election technology tender for 2027 to Smartmatic.

What the IEBC says

At a meeting with political parties on Thursday, November 19, IEBC Commissioner Anne Nderitu said court cases had slowed the buying of election technology and ballot papers, even though tenders had already been advertised, Dawan Africa reported. She said every constituency has at least four registration kits, and that the commission has the time and skills to run a credible election.

Opposition walkout and January deadline

At that same meeting, Gachagua, Wiper leader Kalonzo Musyoka and Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna led opposition leaders out of the room. They said the agenda left out their main concerns, Capital FM and The Standard reported.

Their main demands are:

  • clean the voter register by removing dead and ineligible voters;
  • make constituency results for president final, and end the national tallying centre at Bomas of Kenya;
  • allow electronic voting for Kenyans living abroad;
  • livestream voting, counting and the announcement of results.

Speaking at a church in Runyenjes, Embu County, on Sunday, Gachagua gave the IEBC until January to respond. He warned of nationwide protests if it does not, Dawan Africa reported. He also asked the IEBC to say when it will audit the voter register.

The government side

Interior Cabinet Secretary Kipchumba Murkomen accused the opposition of resisting open tallying of presidential votes. He said the final count must happen at the national tallying centre with candidates' agents present, Capital FM reported. Senate Speaker Moses Wetang'ula urged the IEBC not to be intimidated by political groups.

94 parties must fix their nomination rules

In a separate step, the IEBC said on Friday, November 20, that it had checked the nomination rules of 105 parties. Only 11 passed. The other 94 must make changes, Citizen Digital and Capital FM reported.

The parties that passed include Wiper, Jubilee, Safina and Babu Owino's The Mwananchi Party. Those that must make changes include UDA, ODM, KANU and the Democratic Party, according to Citizen Digital. Kenya Today reported that Gachagua's DCP is also on that list.

The IEBC said parties that failed are not blocked from the 2027 election. Each party has been told what to fix and given a deadline.

What to watch: how the IEBC keeps voter registration running after today, and when the court rules on the technology tender.

stories.title: World roundup: COP31 ends without a deal, Iran tensions stay high, Russia steps up attacks on Ukraine
key_points: UN climate talks in Turkey ended Sunday with no main agreement; COP32 goes to Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.
Fighting between the US and Iran has returned; Trump says he wants a lasting deal.
Zelenskyy asked the US to release Patriot missiles after a week of heavy Russian attacks.
UN peacekeepers in Lebanon are handing their work to the Lebanese army before their mission ends.
stories.content:
Here are the biggest world stories of the weekend, in short and simple form.

1. Climate talks end with no main deal

The UN climate summit, COP31, ended in Antalya, Turkey, on Sunday, November 22, without the main agreement countries were working on, UN News reported. Talks ran two days past the deadline, making it the longest UN climate summit on record.

The big fight was over coal, oil and gas. Countries hit hard by climate change wanted a clear plan to move away from fossil fuels. Big fuel exporters, such as Saudi Arabia and Russia, pushed back, CBS News and other outlets reported. The European Union, Panama and the Marshall Islands rejected the final text.

UN Secretary-General António Guterres called the result a deep disappointment. Ghana, speaking for the African Group, said the text fell short on money for poorer countries but did not block it.

Why it matters for Africa: the next summit, COP32, will be held in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, and will take up the unfinished issues.

2. US–Iran: fighting is back, talk of a deal continues

The US–Iran conflict began on February 28, 2026. A ceasefire and a June agreement followed, but that agreement broke down and fighting returned, Gulf News reported. The two sides exchanged fire again on November 17.

President Donald Trump said the US is talking to Iran and wants a deal that lasts even after he leaves office. He has not shared a plan or a timetable. Meanwhile, Anadolu Agency reported that Bahrain renewed its threat alert, after Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed they had destroyed two US radar systems there. That claim has not been independently confirmed.

3. Ukraine asks for more air defence

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy urged the United States to approve the delivery of Patriot missiles, which can shoot down ballistic missiles, Al Jazeera reported. He said partners have already paid for them.

Zelenskyy said Russia fired about 2,700 drones, nearly 1,460 guided bombs and 165 missiles at Ukraine in one week. On Sunday, a Russian drone attack partly brought down an apartment building in Dymer, near Kyiv, and rescuers were searching for missing people, including children.

4. UN peacekeepers prepare to leave Lebanon

The UN force in southern Lebanon, UNIFIL, has begun handing its duties to the Lebanese army, according to Anadolu Agency. The UN Security Council voted in 2025 to end the mission on December 31, 2026, with troops leaving during 2027. Lebanese leaders have asked for more time, so far without success, the Associated Press reported.

KASS-mtv will keep you updated on these stories.

stories.content:
ALLENTOWN, Pennsylvania — Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna's tour of the United States moved to Pennsylvania on Sunday, November 22, the second day of a 17-day trip to meet Kenyans living in America.

Sifuna leads the Linda Mwananchi Movement (LMM) and has said he will run for president in Kenya's August 2027 election.

A warm welcome

Sifuna landed at Newark Liberty International Airport in New Jersey, where dozens of Kenyans waved flags and chanted as his team arrived, Uzalendo News reported. The Star said supporters broke into song and dance when they saw him.

He is travelling with Vihiga Senator Godfrey Osotsi and former Meru Governor Kawira Mwangaza, according to The Star.

The tour's plan was to open an LMM office in Hackettstown, New Jersey, at noon on Saturday, November 21.

Sunday in Allentown

The published programme for Sunday was:

  • a morning church service at Grace Community Church in Allentown;
  • a town hall meeting at The Palace Center, from 2pm to 6pm.

KASS-mtv had not yet seen reports of what was said at the town hall when this story was written. We will update readers when we do.

Where the tour goes next

  • Nov 23–25: Maryland and the Washington DC area — community dinner, policy meeting, women's brunch, Gen Z meeting and a town hall;
  • Late November: Dallas and Houston, Texas;
  • Early December: Seattle and California, ending on December 7.

Dates have changed before, so check with the organisers before you travel.

Why politicians keep coming to the US

Sifuna is not the first. Democracy for the Citizens Party leader Rigathi Gachagua made a long US tour earlier this year, with stops that included Oregon, Kansas, Dallas, Boston and Spokane, the Nation reported. The Star reported that Wiper leader Kalonzo Musyoka is also planning a US tour.

Analysts say money is a big reason. Political analyst Martin Andati told The Star the tours are mainly about fundraising, because the number of Kenyans living abroad is small compared with voters at home. Prof Kefa Otiso of Bowling Green State University told the Nation that the diaspora also helps politicians by persuading family and friends back home.

The money Kenyans in the US send home

Kenyans in the US are the country's biggest source of money sent home, but that flow has slowed this year. Central Bank of Kenya Governor Kamau Thugge said total remittances fell 1.3% in the 12 months to August 2026, mostly because less money came from the US and Saudi Arabia, Kenyans.co.ke reported. Kenyans.co.ke has also linked part of the slowdown to a new US tax on money transfers.

According to The Rio Times, citing CBK figures, money from the US in October 2026 was about US$178 million, 28% lower than a year earlier.

For Kenyans in America, that makes the coming town halls a chance to ask candidates direct questions about jobs, remittance costs and how the diaspora can vote.

stories.title: Opposition leaders reject 'third force' talk as Gachagua promises Mt Kenya direction before Christmas
key_points: Matiang'i, Nyoro and Karua told a Kirinyaga church on Sunday that the opposition is one team.
They said the opposition will field one presidential candidate, but gave no date or method.
In Embu, Gachagua said he will give Mt Kenya its political direction before Christmas.
Gachagua also asked the IEBC to say when the voter register will be audited.
stories.content:
NAIROBI — Three opposition leaders used a church service in Kirinyaga on Sunday, November 22, to deny reports that they are building a separate "third force" inside the opposition.

At the same time, in neighbouring Embu County, former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua held his own church meeting and set out his plans for the Mt Kenya vote.

What happened in Kirinyaga

Jubilee Party leader Fred Matiang'i, People's Party of Kenya (PPK) leader Ndindi Nyoro and People's Liberation Party (PLP) leader Martha Karua attended a service at Kimunye ACK Church, The Star reported. Kirinyaga is Ms Karua's home county. MPs Anthony Kibagendi (Kitutu South), Clive Gisairo (Kitutu Masaba) and Patrick Osero (Borabu) were also there.

The four leaders, together with Siaya Governor James Orengo, have toured several regions together in recent weeks, including Gusii. The Nation reported that this had fuelled talk of a new power bloc that could shape who the opposition picks as its presidential candidate.

The leaders said that is not true:

  • Nyoro said, according to The Star: "There is only one force in the Opposition." He said the opposition will pick one flagbearer, and that leaders missing from Kirinyaga were meeting supporters in Embu and other places.
  • Matiang'i said the opposition has no time for fighting and accused unnamed people of trying to divide it for their own gain. "We have one team in Kenya in the opposition," he said, as quoted by The Kenya Times.
  • Karua said the leaders' different tours are planned together to win support across the country, and that the opposition will settle on one candidate to face President William Ruto.

According to The Kenya Times, Ms Karua has also said she is ready to step aside and back either Matiang'i or Nyoro if the opposition chooses one of them. The opposition has not yet said how or when it will pick its candidate.

What Gachagua said in Embu

Mr Gachagua, who leads the Democracy for the Citizens Party (DCP), spoke at Wonders of God Church in Karurumo, Runyenjes, People Daily reported. He said:

  • he will give the Mt Kenya region its political direction before Christmas, after months of meetings with residents. The Kenya Times reported the dates as December 22 or 23;
  • families can use the holidays to discuss and agree on the region's preferred candidates;
  • the IEBC should say when it will audit the voter register, and remove dead voters and foreigners he claims are on it. People Daily noted he did not give evidence for the claim about foreigners.

Citizen Digital reported that Mr Gachagua also said opposition leaders now hold key voting regions, naming Mt Kenya for himself, Kisii for Matiang'i and Lower Eastern for Wiper leader Kalonzo Musyoka.

Why it matters

Kenya's next general election is in August 2027. The opposition has many leaders who want to run for president, and every one of them says the group will back a single candidate. How they choose that person is the big question for the coming months.

The IEBC had not publicly responded to Mr Gachagua's demands by the time of writing.
