stories.title: Sifuna brings Linda Mwananchi tour to Kenyans in the US, starting Saturday in New Jersey
key_points: The tour starts Saturday, Nov 21, in Hackettstown, New Jersey, and ends Dec 7 in Silicon Valley, California.
Stops include Pennsylvania, Maryland, Washington DC, Texas, Seattle and California.
Plans include town halls, community dinners and meetings with Gen Z groups.
The dates have changed before, so check with the organisers before you travel.
stories.content:
Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna is taking his Linda Mwananchi Movement to Kenyans in the United States, with a tour that starts this Saturday in New Jersey.

The movement says the tour will open on November 21 with a new Linda Mwananchi office in Hackettstown, New Jersey, at noon, and end in Silicon Valley, California, on December 7.

Where and when (latest published plan)

  • Nov 21, Hackettstown, NJ: office opening at noon
  • Nov 22, Allentown, PA: church service, then a town hall at Palace Center from 2pm to 6pm
  • Nov 23, Maryland: community dinner at Spark Hotel at 7:30pm
  • Nov 24, Washington, DC
  • Nov 27, Dallas, TX
  • Nov 29, Houston, TX
  • Dec 3–4, Seattle area, WA: Renton and Federal Way
  • Dec 5, San Francisco and Oakland, CA
  • Dec 7, Silicon Valley, CA

The plan includes town hall meetings, community dinners, sessions with Gen Z groups and meetings with elected officials, Capital FM reported.

Earlier versions of the schedule were different. A programme reported by the Nation and The Standard in early November had Sifuna arriving in Allentown on November 20 and finishing in Seattle and California by December 4. Please confirm times and venues with the organisers before travelling.

Why the tour matters

Sifuna is seen as a rising challenger to President William Ruto ahead of the August 2027 election. The Nation reported that the trip aims to win over diaspora voters and raise money for his campaign.

Former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua made a similar US trip from August 26 to October 9, with stops including Spokane, Portland, Kansas, Dallas and Boston.

The visit also comes as the money Kenyans abroad send home is slowing down:

  • October: Central Bank of Kenya figures show remittances were $430.5 million in October 2026, down 1.9% from October 2025.
  • 12 months to October: remittances fell 1.1% to $5.023 billion.
  • From the US: money from Kenya's biggest source fell 12.6% in the first half of the year, according to Business Daily. A new US tax on money transfers began on January 1.

stories.title: Ruto starts 8-day Western Kenya tour as poll shows Sifuna ahead in the region
key_points: Ruto is touring all four Western counties: Busia, Kakamega, Vihiga and Bungoma.
A Tifa poll last week put Senator Edwin Sifuna at 55% in Western, against Ruto's 25%.
Ruto launched roads, markets, a cultural centre and electricity connections.
Kenya's next general election is in August 2027.
stories.content:
NAIROBI — President William Ruto has begun an eight-day campaign tour of Western Kenya, a region where a new poll shows Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna well ahead of him.

The tour covers all four Western counties — Busia, Kakamega, Vihiga and Bungoma — and is split into two parts, with rest days in between, The Star reported on Friday.

On Thursday, Ruto was in Busia and Bungoma. In Teso North, Busia, he:

  • opened the Kakapel Cultural Centre;
  • opened new classrooms and offices at Kapkemer Comprehensive Primary School;
  • launched work on the Butula–Nambale–Amukura–Machakusi–Kocholia road;
  • started the Last Mile electricity connection project at Segero Centre.

In Bungoma, he launched two road projects, laid the foundation stone for Bokoli Modern Market and opened Naitiri Modern Market in Tongaren.

On Friday he was due in Budalang'i and Funyula in Busia, then Butere and Shinyalu in Kakamega. Saturday's plan includes Matungu, Sirisia and Vihiga.

Why Western matters now

The trip comes a week after a Tifa poll found 55% support for Sifuna in Western, against 25% for Ruto. Sifuna leads the Linda Mwananchi Movement and is seen as a growing challenger ahead of the 2027 election.

Western has long voted with the late Raila Odinga. Ruto had been expected to win much of that support through his working deal with ODM, but Sifuna's rise has changed the picture. Ruto also needs Western votes to make up for support he may lose in Mt Kenya after his split with former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua.

Speaking in Teso North, Ruto accused his rivals of dividing people along tribal lines and said they have no plans for schools, electricity, roads or health. "Those people, we shall show them dust in the elections," he said.

Several leaders joined him:

  • Prime Cabinet Secretary Musalia Mudavadi;
  • National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang'ula;
  • Cooperatives Cabinet Secretary Wycliffe Oparanya;
  • Busia Governor Paul Otuoma.

Oparanya said ODM remains in the broad-based government and will back Ruto's re-election. Wetang'ula urged a big turnout in August next year.

According to The Star, Ruto has visited about 24 counties in the past two months.

KASS-mtv will follow the rest of the tour.
